title: The Accusation Audit
description: Say their worst thoughts about you first, and they lose their power.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Before a hard conversation, list everything negative the other person might be thinking about you and say it out loud. Naming the criticism before they raise it defuses it.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: An accusation loses force once it has been said. If you voice it first, the other side cannot land it as a blow, and they often soften because you have been candid.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: "You're probably thinking I'm here to squeeze more money out of you."
"You may feel this whole process has been a waste of your time."

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Opening with the other side's likely objections.
Naming your own weaknesses before they can.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Write down every unflattering thing they might believe, then say the strongest ones early and calmly. Do not defend — just name them.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Using an audit to fake humility.
Listing accusations in order to provoke guilt.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Do not let a pre-emptive apology buy a concession.
Keep your original concerns on the table.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Waiting for the attack instead of pre-empting it.
Naming the accusation and then arguing against it.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Say their doubt before they do.
